en.text: In Unit 1 you listened for details about Ethiopia's economy, asked Wh-questions in interviews, read about rural non-farm income, learned words for farming types and money, and used the simple present in the active and passive voice.

screens.title: Unit 1 in brief
paras: Listening: agriculture employs about 80% of workers; fishing is freshwater only; waterpower and forests give energy.
Speaking: Wh-questions (what, where, why, how) get full answers.
Reading: rural families add non-farm work because farm income is seasonal and risky.
Vocabulary: mixed, arable, subsistence, dairy, nomadic farming; income, profit, expense, loss.
Grammar: active "Farmers sell crops" ↔ passive "Crops are sold by farmers".

screens.text: Which sentence correctly uses two words from the unit?
opts: Mixed farming gives the family income from both crops and milk.
Subsistence farming makes a big profit for export.
screens.ans: Mixed farming gives the family income from both crops and milk.
screens.why: Mixed farming = crops + livestock, so income from both is correct. The others contradict the definitions.
